re_line: Kim snubs Trump meeting · Education minister resigns over AI cheating · KOSPI plunges 5.21% · WSJ/ArmsControlWonk: Yongbyon enrichment expansion confirmed · DP targets chief justice impeachment by December
morning_memo: Kim Jong Un spurned Trump's meeting offer during the Asia trip, visiting educational factory sites instead.
Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin resigned; President Lee accepted his offer within one hour over AI cheating chaos ahead of the Suneung.
KOSPI fell 5.21% on November 20 on AI selloff fears; government activated market stabilization fund preparations.

key_stat.label: ROK car trade deficit with China, Jan-Oct 2026 (record high)
key_stat.context: South Korea's car trade deficit with China hit a record in the first ten months of 2026, driven by a 79.2% surge in China-made car imports, led by Tesla Gigafactory Shanghai vehicles, while Korean exports to China fell 34.9%.

imagery_report.label: New satellite imagery: Yongbyon uranium enrichment expansion confirmed
imagery_report.headline: New satellite photos show expansion of North Korea's uranium enrichment plant at Yongbyon
imagery_report.body: The Wall Street Journal published new satellite imagery showing expansion of North Korea's uranium enrichment facility at Yongbyon. ArmsControlWonk published accompanying analysis by Jeffrey Lewis, noting a small addition to Yongbyon's original uranium enrichment plant (UEP), with Lewis's comments cited in the WSJ piece by Anika Seth and Ashley Cai.

bp_locations.name: Yongbyon Nuclear Complex
bp_locations.note: As of April 2026: Enrichment building expansion complete, new centrifuge hall operational. 5 MWe reactor and IRT-2000 both running. Thermal signatures consistent with increased plutonium/HEU production.

bp_locations.name: Sinpo South Shipyard
bp_locations.note: As of May 2025: Hero Kim Kun Ok SLBM submarine exited drydock after more than two years of fitting-out but was still not operational. New submarine construction begun in separate bay. NK Pro satellite analysis (Oct 20 2026) separately reports North Korea's Nampho Shipyard missed a deadline earlier in Oct 2026 to launch a 5,000-ton naval destroyer, with hull sections visible at two potential outdoor assembly areas. 38 North analysis published Oct 30 documents public display of a vessel described as a 'Tactical Nuclear Attack' submarine. Kim Jong Un inspected Nampho Shipyard on Nov 7 (reported Nov 8 by KCNA), announcing a new warship under construction larger than the destroyer built last year. NK News reported on Nov 6 that North Korea has expanded warship construction to a third shipyard. 38 North published analysis on Nov 11 of the Choe Hyon destroyer and its strategic implications for the West Sea Fleet. NK News identified a second major east-coast naval base project on Nov 13, beyond the Munchon-area site Kim inspected on Nov 12.

bp_locations.name: THAAD Site, Seongju County
bp_locations.note: As of March 2026: All 6 THAAD launchers were redeployed to the Middle East amid Iran tensions. At least 2 launchers may have returned to Seongju by late March 2026. Battery operational status remains uncertain. This report is from March 2026 and may not reflect the current state.

bp_locations.name: Sohae Satellite Launch Station
bp_locations.note: As of March 2026: 2,500 kN engine test stand firing observed. Two villages razed for facility expansion. New seaport and large assembly building nearing completion. This report is from March 2026 and may not reflect the current state.

bp_locations.name: Punggye-ri Nuclear Test Site
bp_locations.note: As of November 2025: ROK Defense Intelligence Agency assessed Tunnel No. 3 is test-ready and a nuclear test can be conducted at any time upon political decision. Site maintained at high readiness since mid-2024. This report is from November 2025 and may not reflect the current state.

bp_locations.name: Tumangang–Khasan (NK-Russia border)
bp_locations.note: As of March 2026: Road bridge construction accelerated, completion target moved to Summer 2026. Passenger rail service resumed mid-2025. Ore and tank car traffic at highest levels since project began. This report is from March 2026 and may not reflect the current state. Russian Transport Ministry applications filed November 13, 2026 for a 14-daily-round-trip Vladivostok-Rason bus route over the new vehicle bridge, with experts noting the service will likely transport DPRK workers more than Russian tourists.

bp_locations.name: Sinuiju–Dandong (NK-China border)
bp_locations.note: NK News Planet Labs satellite imagery analyzed through November 15, 2026 confirms trucks filling Sinuiju customs facility from October 16, the day after the New Yalu River Bridge officially opened, with activity peaking October 19–20. A wall of 40-foot containers bearing Maersk and COSCO markings was visible on the Chinese side. Kim Jong Un crossed the New Yalu River Bridge on October 24 during his unannounced visit to Dandong. Daily NK reported November 12 that Chinese truck drivers who relied on side income ferrying parcels across the new bridge are souring on operations due to tighter customs checks and movement controls. Huanghai Automobile's Dandong bus factory announced November 13 it is operating at full capacity following Kim Jong Un's October visit. Daily NK reported November 18 that Sinuiju markets are overflowing with Chinese goods but a severe cash shortage means almost nobody is buying, with vendors describing a 'trading cliff.'

bp_locations.name: Rason SEZ
bp_locations.note: As of November 2025: Chinese businesspeople re-entry to Rason SEZ expanded. Coal exports through Rason at highest levels in years throughout 2025. Arms export berth also active. This report is from November 2025 and may not reflect the current state.

bp_locations.name: Yellow Sea NLL
bp_locations.note: As of September 26, 2025: 140m DPRK merchant vessel Toksong crossed the Northern Limit Line near Baengnyeong Island, advanced 5km south. ROK Navy fired approximately 60 warning shots; vessel retreated after 1 hour. ROK Marine Corps Commandant Gen. Ju Il-suk stated October 20, 2026 that North Korea has made 'various changes' to forces facing South Korea's border islands, with Seoul stepping up surveillance along the maritime border. 38 North satellite imagery published October 29 shows North Korea continuing to install new fencing along its border. North Korean propaganda loudspeakers were visible at two border locations on November 4, 2026 from Odusan Unification Observatory and Key Observatory in Gyeonggi Province. ROK Joint Chiefs confirmed November 6, 2026 that a drifting North Korean fishing vessel was spotted in international waters off Ulleung Island on November 3 and is under investigation.

bp_locations.name: Yellow Sea PMZ
bp_locations.note: As of January 27-28, 2026: Atlantic Amsterdam (converted oil rig, Chinese aquaculture platform) relocated out of the Provisional Measures Zone to Weihai shipyard following President Lee Jae-myung's Beijing state visit. Two giant aquaculture cages (Shen Lan 1, Shen Lan 2) and 13 buoys remain in the PMZ. This report is from January 2026 and may not reflect the current state.

bp_locations.name: Vostochny/Dunai
bp_locations.note: As of January 2026: Arms shipments slowed due to ice, one Russian vessel (likely Angara or Lady R) visited Rason, docked January 14, 2026 at arms export berth. Cargo routed to Vostochny. Since September 2023: 64 voyages by 4 vessels (Angara, Maria, Maya-1, Lady R) delivered approximately 15,800 containers (approximately 4.2-5.8 million munitions) from Rajin to Vostochny/Dunai. This report is from January 2026 and may not reflect the current state. Russian Transport Ministry applications filed November 13, 2026 for a Vladivostok-Rason bus route operating 14 daily round trips.

top_stories.headline: Kim Jong Un spurned Trump's meeting offer; Trump administration had explored Korean War end declaration to secure a summit
top_stories.body: **Kim Jong Un** declined to meet President **Donald Trump** during Trump's Asia trip, with Yonhap and the WSJ reporting the Trump administration actively pursued a summit and had explored various inducements, including a Korean War end-of-war declaration, with North Korea ultimately presenting conditions Washington found unacceptable. Trump said at a press conference that the meeting 'didn't work out' but vowed to 'have that meeting' in the future; North Korea's state media made no reference to the offer. Kim instead conducted a publicized inspection of educational factory sites, the dominant domestic image of the day.

top_stories.headline: Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin resigns over AI cheating chaos ahead of Suneung; Lee accepts within one hour
top_stories.body: **Choi Kyo-jin** resigned as education minister on November 22, one hour after announcing his intention to step down over last-minute anti-AI-cheating rules that caused widespread confusion ahead of the College Scholastic Ability Test (Suneung) held November 19. President **Lee Jae-myung** formally approved the dismissal and instructed Prime Minister **Han Seong-sook** to take full responsibility for follow-up measures; Lee posted on X that 'the fairness of exams is a principle that cannot be compromised.' The People Power Party leader **Jang Dong-hyuk** said the minister's resignation was insufficient and demanded the government explain the root cause of the failure.

top_stories.headline: New satellite imagery confirms additional expansion at Yongbyon uranium enrichment plant
top_stories.body: New commercial satellite photos published by the WSJ and analyzed by **Jeffrey Lewis** at ArmsControlWonk show a small but concrete addition to North Korea's original uranium enrichment plant (UEP) at Yongbyon, separate from the previously reported new centrifuge hall expansion. The imagery corroborates the sustained upward trend in enrichment-related construction at the complex that analysts have tracked through 2026. North Korea's nuclear program is expanding as Trump, Xi Jinping, and Vladimir Putin held their first trilateral summit in Shenzhen, at which Trump said Korean Peninsula dangers were discussed.

top_stories.headline: KOSPI plunges 5.21% on November 20; government convenes emergency 'F4' meeting and prepares market stabilization fund
top_stories.body: The KOSPI closed November 20 down *5.21%* at 4,869.96, breaching the 5,000 level, after a global AI-sector selloff triggered by NVIDIA's stock rout, with sell-side circuit breakers (saiducar) activated. Deputy Prime Minister **Lee Hyung-il** convened an emergency inter-agency meeting that afternoon with Financial Services Commission Chairman **Lee Eok-won**, Financial Supervisory Service Director **Lee Chan-jin**, and Bank of Korea Governor **Shin Hyun-song** to prepare activation of the market stabilization fund (jeunganpendo) and ease daily share buyback limits for three months effective November 24. Goldman Sachs' panic index reached 9 out of 10, per Bloomberg, with foreign net selling of Korean equities totaling 45 trillion won over September-October.

also_today.body_text: Despite Pyongyang construction projects, most North Koreans face deepening poverty and market shortages, with a widening gap between elite consumption and mass deprivation.

also_today.body_text: Seoul and Jakarta are urged to operationalize a bilateral AI cooperation agreement within two years, alongside clean energy and infrastructure partnerships.

also_today.headline: China's Ministry of State Security running two-year covert operation to acquire advanced semiconductors, circumventing US export controls
also_today.body_text: China's Ministry of State Security has operated a dedicated unit for more than two years to procure advanced AI semiconductors by circumventing US export bans, reporting directly to MSS chief Chen Yixin, according to current and former US officials cited by the New York Times.

us_korea_deals.state_of_play: Steel and aluminum remain at 50% and automobiles at 15%, both under Section 232. The Section 122 surcharge expired July 24, so no single baseline reciprocal tariff applies. Section 301 is now the primary prospective vehicle for new tariff measures on South Korea.

business_economy.headline: FSC Chairman Lee Eok-won travels to Europe, signs bank supervision MOU with the European Central Bank
business_economy.body_text: Financial Services Commission Chairman **Lee Eok-won** signed a memorandum of understanding on bank supervisory cooperation with the European Central Bank during a European visit, expanding Korea's financial regulatory coordination ahead of potential global financial stability discussions.

northeast_asia.headline: 62% of Japanese feel affinity toward South Korea, record high; 93% say China-Japan relations are bad
northeast_asia.body_text: A Japanese survey found 62% of respondents feel close or friendly toward South Korea, the highest figure recorded; 93% described China-Japan relations as poor. The divergence in Japanese attitudes toward Seoul and Beijing comes as Japan PM Takaichi Sanae reaffirmed the 'one China' policy while China maintained a hardline stance.

northeast_asia.headline: Quincy Institute: Trump's honeymoon with South Korea is over as alliance tensions mount
northeast_asia.body_text: The Quincy Institute argues that despite early personal rapport between Trump and Lee, friction has accumulated over the $350B investment pace, defense spending targets, and Korea's handling of the North Korea file, with both governments acknowledging 'turbulence.' The piece cites the US ambassador's October 21 statements as a turning point.

northeast_asia.headline: Unification Minister Chung Dong-young visits Panmunjom with United Nations Command Commander Gen. Xavier Brunson
northeast_asia.body_text: Unification Minister **Chung Dong-young** visited Panmunjom accompanied by United Nations Command (UNC) Commander **Gen. Xavier Brunson**, days after Chung met the new US ambassador; the joint visit follows reported 'turbulence' in the US-ROK alliance.

gallup_spotlight.finding: 47% of respondents cited the economy as the most important issue heading into future elections, with the Democratic Party holding a lead in party preference despite economic anxieties.

rok_government.action: President Lee accepts Education Minister's resignation; orders exam fairness measures
rok_government.detail: President Lee accepted Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin's resignation within one hour of its announcement and formally approved the dismissal. Lee instructed Prime Minister Han Seong-sook to take full responsibility for follow-up and ordered law reforms to block exam-room photo transmission, posting on X that exam fairness 'cannot be compromised.'

rok_government.ministry: Ministry of Science and ICT / korea.kr
rok_government.action: Government fast-tracks AI data center permitting with batch approval and assessment exemptions
rok_government.detail: Korea.kr announced new regulations enabling batch processing of permits and assessment exemptions for AI data center construction, accelerating deployment timelines for planned facilities.

calendar_watch.headline: 2026 Development Cooperation Week opens
calendar_watch.detail: The Office for Government Policy Coordination launches the 2026 Korea ODA Development Cooperation Week (Nov 23-27), coinciding with the November 25 International Development Cooperation Day marking Korea's 2009 OECD DAC accession.

calendar_watch.headline: Justice Minister nominee Lee Yong-cheol confirmation hearing
calendar_watch.detail: Justice Minister nominee Lee Yong-cheol faces a National Assembly confirmation hearing, where opposition members have pressed him to answer yes or no on whether he would order withdrawal of charges against President Lee Jae-myung.

calendar_watch.headline: Ruling party retirement-age special committee deadline
calendar_watch.detail: The ruling Democratic Party faces a November 27 deadline for its special committee on retirement-age extension to reach a conclusion; the labor minister stated the government will announce its own plan if no agreement is reached.

rok_assembly.committee: Democratic Merit Persons Act, Full Assembly
rok_assembly.action: National Assembly passes Democratic Merit Persons Act after 26-year legislative effort
rok_assembly.detail: The National Assembly passed the Democratic Merit Persons Act, extending medical, care and welfare support to 635 recognized democracy movement figures including Jeon Tae-il, Park Jong-cheol and Lee Han-yeol; the legislation also advances national management of the former May 18 Gwangju cemetery.

rok_assembly.action: JTBC reports Serious Crimes Investigation Agency's first corporate investigation faces 'collateral charge' allegations; prosecution and courts rejecting cases
rok_assembly.detail: JTBC's exclusive report says the Serious Crimes Investigation Agency's inaugural major corporate probe is generating 'collateral charge' allegations, with the prosecution and courts repeatedly rejecting filings in the case, complicating the new agency's operational credibility.

rok_personnel.name: Choi Kyo-jin
rok_personnel.detail: Choi Kyo-jin resigned as education minister on November 22 and President Lee formally approved the dismissal after last-minute anti-AI-cheating rules caused chaos ahead of the November 19 Suneung. Lee instructed Prime Minister Han Seong-sook to manage follow-up; a successor nomination process will proceed through standard procedures.

opeds_today.headline: Trump-Xi-Putin Summit: What Happened? | The Capital Cable #147
opeds_today.central_argument: The Trump-Xi-Putin Shenzhen summit produced a four-point peace declaration whose implications for the Korean Peninsula remain uncertain, particularly after Kim Jong Un declined to attend despite Trump's suggestion he might.
opeds_today.summary: Victor Cha and Sydney Seiler join host Mark Lippert to unpack what the three leaders agreed to, what the declaration means for the Korean Peninsula, and why Kim Jong Un stayed away.

opeds_today.source: CSIS | Center for Strategic and International Studies
opeds_today.headline: ASEAN Outcomes and Trump's Manila Visit
opeds_today.central_argument: Trump's participation in the Manila ASEAN Summit and Quad meeting, followed by his stop in Shenzhen, sets new parameters for US-China competition and Indo-Pacific multilateral engagement.
opeds_today.summary: The analysis examines what happened at the ASEAN Summit, East Asia Summit, Quad, and Trump's bilateral meetings with the Philippines and Thailand, and how those outcomes will affect US-China competition.

kcna_delta.kim_activity: Kim Jong Un received credentials in person from Andrei Leonidovich Podolshev, the new Russian ambassador to North Korea, a protocol change described as the first such direct reception in over 30 years.

top_articles.headline: Police officers clash publicly over trader at Hyesan Station, exposing bribery system
top_articles.summary: Two North Korean police officers got into a public shouting match outside Hyesan Station in November 2026 over a trader lacking a travel permit, drawing a crowd and exposing a railway police bribery network.

top_articles.headline: Kangdong County Hospital approaches first anniversary with improved facilities but ongoing gaps
top_articles.summary: Pyongyang's Kangdong County Hospital is functioning better than other county facilities after nearly one year, with some patients paying less under North Korea's rolling health insurance system, but supply and staffing gaps persist.

kcna_delta.bottom_line: State media's dominant image was Kim's direct receipt of the Russian ambassador's credentials, an unusual protocol shift, while domestic content covered light industry and social welfare; the failed Trump summit offer remained absent from KCNA output.

capitol_hill.headline: Midterms gave US-South Korea alliance new defenders in Congress, though turbulence remains
capitol_hill.body_text: The midterm Democratic wave brought new members sympathetic to the US-South Korea alliance into Congress, but structural tensions over the $350B investment pace and defense spending targets persist; both governments have acknowledged 'turbulence' in the relationship.

capitol_hill.headline: US senators say a Trump-Kim summit is unlikely for the foreseeable future
capitol_hill.body_text: US senators told VOA Korean that a US-North Korea summit is unlikely in the near term following Kim Jong Un's refusal to meet Trump during the Asia trip, with conditions North Korea set proving unacceptable to Washington.

korea_world.headline: South Korean army transfers K9 Thunder howitzer expertise to Poland, laying groundwork for expanded Eastern Europe exports
korea_world.body_text: The South Korean Army is transferring K9 Thunder howitzer operational expertise to Poland, deepening the defense export relationship that has made Poland ROK's largest European arms customer and laying groundwork for further Eastern European sales.

korea_world.headline: Saudi Arabia turns to South Korea and others for air-defense systems to counter drone and missile attacks
korea_world.body_text: Saudi Arabia is diversifying its air-defense procurement to include South Korean suppliers amid ongoing drone and missile threats, expanding ROK's defense export footprint in the Gulf region.

korea_world.headline: Korean consortium wins Vietnam high-speed rail design contract
korea_world.body_text: A South Korean consortium secured the design contract for Vietnam's high-speed rail project, extending Seoul's overseas infrastructure export push and deepening Korea-Vietnam economic ties.
